title: orchestrated-rollback-runway-and-customer-escallation-bundle-for-cross-tier-canary-failure
creator: Aisha Nair
description: Summary: Create a repeatable, low-friction rollback runway that bundles a hotfix, cross-tier traffic control, and a customer-facing escalation path when model rollouts cause degraded quality or latency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket captures: playbook steps, operator commands, automated gating checks, customer comms templates, and a small shim service to perform safe partial-traffic pins and KV cache reconciliation across variants. Goal: reduce mean time to safe-state (MTTS) for canary regressions to under 20 minutes for P0 incidents and provide a clear, auditable path for customer liaison teams.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can pin traffic to previous model variant for a single tenant without global outage via a single CLI command
KV cache reconciliation actions documented and scripted for both in-memory and Redis-backed caches
Automated gating verifies response-sampling schema (JSON LLM output) and regression score before allowing rollout reattempt
Customer liaison template in place and validated with Legal/Support for P0 communications
Runbook validated in a fire-drill with SRE, Platform, and Support within the cycle
runbook_steps: Triage: confirm regression signature with sampling dashboard (dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.ai/rollouts/summary)
Impact assessment: list affected deployment types and tenants using query: SELECT tenant, deployment_type FROM rollout_events WHERE variant != baseline LIMIT 100
Contain: execute partial pin for affected tenant(s) with CLI: rwctl pin --tenant=<TENANT_ID> --model=<BASELINE_MODEL> --percent=100
KV cache reconcile: run helper script to mark stale prefices and rehydrate: ./scripts/kvcache_reconcile.sh --tenants <TENANT_ID_LIST>
If dedicated/private: run on-prem agent handshake: ssh ops@<customer-host> 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && sudo /usr/local/bin/rw-agent reconcile-keys --variant <BASELINE>'
Communication: notify customer via template, open incident bridge (#ops-bridge) and set expectation window
Post-mortem: capture PR links, timeline, and decision rationale in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Canary+Rollback+Runway
operator_commands: Pin traffic: rwctl pin --tenant T-1234 --target-variant redwood-v1.18 --reason "canary-quality-drop"
Force KV flush for tenant slice: redis-cli -h cache-host -p 6379 --eval scripts/flush_tenant.lua , T-1234
Check variant health: curl -s -XGET 'https://api.redwood.ai/internal/variant-health?variant=redwood-v1.19' | jq '.errors | length'
On-prem handshake (privates): scp ./hotfix.tar ops@<host>:/tmp && ssh ops@<host> 'sudo tar -xvf /tmp/hotfix.tar -C /opt/redwood && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime'
implementation_notes: We will implement a small orchestration shim (Go) to sequence pin/unpin + kvcache reconciliation and emit audit events to event-store

Shim will expose a single atomic endpoint /v1/rollback with JSON body: {tenant, from_variant, to_variant, scope: [models|kv|routing]} (backwards compatibility: legacy CLI translates to endpoint calls)
Plan B for inaccessible private environments: provide ops-run instructions for customer Success to execute with an agent script and remote approval token
We will add feature flags so the shim is initially enabled for a subset of tenants (pilot) and then ramped
risk_assessment: Moderate. Key risks: partial cache divergence causing ephemeral hallucinations after rollback, incorrect pinning that routes other tenants (mitigated by tenant-scoped pins and preflight checks), and customer private-host access delays. Mitigations are included in runbook and preflight automated checks.
